source.title: Are Single-Token Sparse Autoencoder Features Causally Necessary? Layer-Depth and SAE-Family Effects
source.authors: Seonglae Cho; Ze-Kun Wu; Kleyton da Costa; Rishi Kalra; Ilham Wicaksono; A. Koshiyama

record.tranche_reason: The study measures single-token and polysemantic sparse-autoencoder features, not individual neurons or the neuron-level behaviors named in the claim versions. Its results are relevant to SAE-feature interpretation but do not test a listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own SAE-feature measurements, including feature detection sensitivity and differences between detected single-token and polysemantic features. These are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version; they are not neuron-level claim results.
record.test_reason: The study measures SAE features (single-token vs a 'polysemantic' complement defined by activation thresholds) in residual-stream SAEs, not MLP neurons or vision neurons. It invokes superposition only as background. No result bears on whether model neurons are polysemantic or why, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct: zero-ablating single-token SAE features lowers the target-token logit in 178/208 layer conditions; depth determines whether damage cascades downstream or acts on output; on the same base model GemmaScope/BatchTopK features are causally anchored while LlamaScope features are locally redundant; activation function alone does not explain this, so SAE family/training recipe must be treated as an experimental variable.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SAE-feature detection, geometry, and causal ablation rather than reproducing a neuron-visualization or neuron-ablation method from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE-feature detection counts vary with gap and purity thresholds and with the top-k token cache window; the paper notes that its k=20 count is from a different export than the k=5, 7, and 10 sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-token SAE feature counts in GPT2-Small vary strongly with gap/purity thresholds (7,171 to 148) and top-k cache window.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prevalence of single-token (monosemantic) SAE features depends on detection thresholds and cache window.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-token SAE features are more top-token concentrated (92% vs 34%) and cluster 4.7x tighter in decoder space than the polysemantic complement in GPT2-Small L0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-token and polysemantic SAE features differ in activation concentration and decoder geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-token SAE feature prevalence differs 46x between GemmaScope and LlamaScope at 8-9B and declines with model scale within GemmaScope/res-jb; insensitive to SAE activation function at Gemma-2-2B L12 (0.92-0.99%, except Gated/P-Anneal).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Monosemantic SAE feature prevalence depends on SAE family and model scale more than SAE activation function.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Evidence relevant to the claim is indirect because the paper studies SAE features rather than neurons. The authors state that cross-family comparisons co-vary training data, dictionary width, recipe, and post-hoc conversion; some comparisons are descriptive and the scale trend has only three data points. The top-k sensitivity sweep also compares re-exported k=5–10 counts with a k=20 count from the original export.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from the paper were included because its remaining analyses concern SAE-feature geometry, prevalence across SAE families, causal ablation, token categories, or SAE training comparisons, none of which directly tests the neuron-level claim versions.

untested.parts: No MLP neurons measured; subjects are residual-stream SAE features.
Superposition cited as background only; not tested.
Architecture comparisons concern SAE families/activation functions and single-token SAE feature prevalence, not neuron polysemanticity in the base model.
Threshold sensitivity concerns SAE-feature single-token detection, not neuron classification.

record.verdict_notes: 'Polysemantic' here means SAE features failing single-token thresholds, not polysemantic neurons. Paper is not an original source. Rows are all detection/selection or validation numbers; none link to a version.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifiers or vision neurons are studied.
No MLP neurons in language models are measured; the subjects are SAE features.
The paper invokes the superposition hypothesis as background for SAEs but does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by capacity pressure.
No neuron polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise is tested.
Comparisons concern SAE families and SAE-feature causal effects, not the share of polysemantic neurons or neuron-level performance costs.
No canonical polysemantic neurons are examined to determine whether their inputs share a feature.
The paper varies measurement criteria for SAE-feature detection, not the activation range or explanation scoring used to classify individual neurons.
